clue.text: Triumph when surrounded by independent, select group

indicators.note: the word for triumph is placed with the abbreviation for independent wrapped around it

parts.note: IND is the standard abbreviation for independent, as of a politician
to crow is to exult or triumph over someone

explanation.surface: A victorious party celebrates among an exclusive, independent-minded clique.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclusive clique of fashionable insiders is a select group of people.

clue.text: Examine heartless, wretched person

indicators.note: the central letter of the examine word is removed, taking its heart

parts.note: to inspect is to examine

explanation.surface: Someone scrutinises a cruel, despicable individual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle P from INSPECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a bug or creepy-crawly is a contemptuous term for a worthless, despicable person.

clue.text: Wife, excellent, raised lots of concerns

parts.note: a consort is a spouse, especially of a monarch

indicators.note: in a down clue the excellent letters are lifted to read upwards

parts.note: A1 (AI) means first-rate or excellent

explanation.surface: A splendid wife brings up a lot of worries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns AI into IA, read upward in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Groups of businesses working together are associations, and concerns means businesses.

clue.text: In several weeks work one may use a lot of ink

definitions.text: one may use a lot of ink

parts.note: October is a month, several weeks long, abbreviated Oct
an opus is a musical or literary work

explanation.surface: A writer's work spanning weeks uses a lot of ink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'several weeks' is a month, OCT.
explanation.definitionFit: This eight-armed sea creature squirts ink to escape predators, so it uses ink.

clue.text: I fear the worst, but army does nothing wrong

indicators.note: the letters go wrong, being jumbled into a fresh order

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A pessimist worries even though the army does nothing wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges ARMY, DOES and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A pessimist predicting disaster might say of themselves that they expect calamity.

clue.text: Bit of skin trimmed and left in freezer

parts.note: to trim hair or nails is to cut them

indicators.note: the letter for left is placed inside the word for what a freezer makes

parts.note: ice is what a freezer makes, standing in for it here

explanation.surface: A sliver of skin has been snipped off and left in the freezer, an unappetising kitchen discovery.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin layer of skin at the base of a fingernail is a small piece of skin.

clue.text: Heard vulgar call from the hatch

indicators.note: the vulgar word is spoken, and a different spelling sounds the same

parts.note: cheap means tawdry or vulgar

explanation.surface: A coarse shout is heard from a serving hatch.
explanation.walkthrough: The hatch is not a serving hatch but a hatching of chicks.
explanation.definitionFit: Newly hatched chicks make a thin, high cry.

clue.text: Sound quality: pound, shake this

parts.note: timbre is the characteristic quality of a sound
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from libra

explanation.surface: A musician tests sound quality: thump it, rattle it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an instruction: you shake a tambourine.
explanation.definitionFit: An old tambourine-like percussion instrument is played by being shaken or struck.

clue.text: Not much comfort in clubs: not all dance

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

indicators.note: the dance word loses its final letter, so not all of it is used

parts.note: the rumba is a Cuban dance

explanation.surface: Little comfort found in nightclubs where not everyone dances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not all' trims RUMBA to RUMB; a crumb of comfort is a tiny amount.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom a crumb of comfort means only a scrap of consolation.

clue.text: Out of the Top Ten for Armistice Day?

definitions.meaning: the position just below tenth place, just missing a top ten list
the First World War armistice fell at 11am on 11 November, so the day of the month is the number after ten

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Armistice Day as an example: 11 November.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinal after tenth describes both the place just outside a top ten and the date of the armistice.

clue.text: Complaint unlikely in small Shetland island, or round Skye regularly?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes
Unst is the most northerly of the Shetland Islands

indicators.note: the little word or is turned round to read backwards
taking every other letter of Skye, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Wonders whether heat illness is unlikely in the chilly Shetlands or the Hebridean isle of Skye.
explanation.walkthrough: Shetland and Skye are cool, cloudy Scottish islands, which is why the illness is called unlikely there.
explanation.definitionFit: Heat illness from too much sun is an ailment, and complaint means an illness.

clue.text: Colourful sort of light in West

indicators.note: the light abbreviation sits inside the actress's first name

parts.note: Mae West was the Hollywood actress, so West gives her first name
UV stands for ultraviolet light

explanation.surface: A vivid kind of lighting seen somewhere in the western world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' looks like a direction but is the Hollywood actress.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale purple shade is a colour, so the adjective describes something coloured.

clue.text: Problem breathing oxygen after run in competition

indicators.note: the run and oxygen letters are put inside the word for a competition

parts.note: a cup is a knockout competition, such as the FA Cup

indicators.note: oxygen is placed following the run letter

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: An athlete struggles for oxygen after a run in a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts O following R, and 'in' places RO inside CUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A childhood respiratory illness with a barking cough makes breathing difficult.

clue.text: Not quite understand teaching story that can be analysed

indicators.note: the word for understand loses its final letter, so it is not quite complete

parts.note: to see is to understand, as in I see
a parable is a story that teaches a moral lesson

explanation.surface: A student nearly grasps a moral tale whose meaning can be unpicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the last E of SEE, leaving SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something capable of being split into parts can be broken down, which is to be analysed.

clue.text: Objective for Trappists, perhaps, not to exaggerate

definitions.meaning: Trappist monks keep vows of silence, so their aim is to utter as little as possible
a phrase used to signal understatement, admitting the truth is stronger

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is taken literally: silent monks aim to say minimally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom introduces an understatement, the opposite of overstating something.

clue.text: Comes with spikes: singular recipe for losing speed?

parts.note: has means comes with, as a meal has chips
tines are the spikes or prongs of a fork or antler
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A dish arrives with spikes: a single instruction for how to slow down.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the proverb 'more haste, less speed': rushing loses time.
explanation.definitionFit: Rushing too much makes mistakes, so excess speed leads to going slower overall.

clue.text: Companion and I must visit sea-coast for a swim

indicators.note: the letters go for a swim, floating into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A friend and I must visit the seaside for a dip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a swim' rearranges I and SEACOAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner or colleague is a companion.

clue.text: With this telescope, secretly watch grand girl

parts.note: to spy is to watch secretly
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
a lass is a girl, especially in Scotland and northern England

explanation.surface: A peeping Tom uses a telescope to watch a fine young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A small handheld telescope is a pocket instrument for seeing far away.

clue.text: Black music heard in stages that give one a lift

indicators.note: the sound-alike word sits inside the word for stages, before its final letter

parts.note: platforms are raised stages

indicators.note: the music genre is spoken, and the spoken word matches a different spelling

parts.note: soul is a genre of Black American music

explanation.surface: Soul music is played at venues that lift the audience's spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun phrase: (things) that give one a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick-soled 1970s shoes raise the wearer's height, literally giving them a lift.

clue.text: Feminine coiffures repelling husband? Be reasonable!

indicators.note: the coiffure word drives out the husband letter

parts.note: hairdos are coiffures, styled haircuts

explanation.surface: Women with elaborate hairstyles push their husbands away and urge fairness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repelling' drops H from HAIRDOS. The answer is a British plea: 'fair do's!' means 'be fair!'
explanation.definitionFit: The British exclamation demands fair treatment, an appeal to be fair to someone.

clue.text: Start to burn as cheek punched by nasty thug

indicators.note: the cheek word is struck into, with something driven inside it

parts.note: lip means cheek, impudence

indicators.note: the thug letters turn nasty and are mixed up

explanation.surface: A face starts to sting as a vicious thug punches it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges the thug letters, which then go inside the cheek word after its I.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignite a cigarette or fire is to make it begin to burn.

clue.text: Investigate precise moment pressure dropped in game

indicators.note: the trimmed moment goes inside the game word

parts.note: Go is the Asian board game

indicators.note: the pressure letter is dropped from the moment word

parts.note: a point is a precise moment in time
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: An inquiry probes the moment a team let the pressure off during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine a matter in detail is to look into it.

clue.text: I see endless loot around failed invasion site

indicators.note: the whole string is turned around to read backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: the word for loot loses its last letter

parts.note: to pillage is to loot or plunder

explanation.surface: Someone surveys plunder near the site of a disastrous invasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts PILLAGE to PILLAG; 'around' reverses ILOPILLAG to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1915 Allied landings on this Turkish peninsula were a costly failure of the First World War.

clue.text: One city has merged into another

indicators.note: the word has is merged into the middle of the other city

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles, another city

explanation.surface: One city has absorbed another in a municipal merger.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Tibet is a city.

clue.text: The last round — great!

parts.note: O is round in shape
mega is slang for great

explanation.surface: An excited cheer for the final round of a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: The final letter of the Greek alphabet is used to mean the end or last of anything.

clue.text: Travel round city, and finally ask for wall sticker

indicators.note: the travel word goes around the city letters plus the last letter

parts.note: to go is to travel
EC is the postcode for the City of London

indicators.note: picks the last letter of the word ask

explanation.surface: A traveller tours a city and at last asks for a wall decal.
explanation.walkthrough: The City of London's postal district gives the city letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This small lizard has adhesive toe pads, so it clings to walls.

clue.text: Custody, after a court decision

indicators.note: the custody word follows the letter a in the answer

parts.note: being in ward means being in custody or guardianship

explanation.surface: A custody ruling comes after a court decision in a family case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places WARD following A.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge or tribunal may grant damages, and that granted sum is a ruling of a court.

clue.text: Disturbed serenity, receiving a tired look

indicators.note: the shuffled letters take in the letter a
the calm word is disturbed, so its letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's calm is shattered and they wear a weary expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbed' rearranges SERENITY into EYESTRIN, and 'receiving' takes A into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatigue of the visual organs from too much reading or screen time shows as a weary gaze.

clue.text: Clinics, each covering western city

indicators.note: the clinic word wraps around the letter for western

parts.note: sans is short for sanatoriums, health clinics

explanation.surface: Every clinic serves a western city.
explanation.walkthrough: The city is in south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A port in south Wales is a city.

clue.text: Leader to drink more, getting drunk

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: the word more is made drunk, staggering into a new order

explanation.surface: A boss drinks more and becomes intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting drunk' rearranges MORE into REMO.
explanation.definitionFit: A supreme head or overall boss of an organisation is its leader.
